exercise_group.instruction: Use Cramer’s rule to compute the solutions of the systems in Exercises 1–6.
In Exercises 7–10, determine the values of the parameter $$s$$ for which the system has a unique solution, and describe the solution.
In Exercises 11–16, compute the adjugate of the given matrix, and then use Theorem 8 to give the inverse of the matrix.

problem.paragraph: $$\left[\right. 3 & 5 & 4 1 & 0 & 1 2 & 1 & 1 \left]\right.$$
Show that if $$A$$ is $$2 \times 2$$ , then Theorem 8 gives the same formula for $$A^{- 1}$$ as that given by Theorem 4 in Section 2.2.
Suppose that all the entries in $$A$$ are integers and $$\det A = 1$$ . Explain why all the entries in $$A^{- 1}$$ are integers.

exercise_group.instruction: In Exercises 19–22, find the area of the parallelogram whose vertices are listed.

problem.paragraph: $$\left( {0, - 2} \right)$$ , $$\left( 5, - \left. 2 \right) \right.$$ , $${( -}3{,}1)$$ , $$\left(\right. 2 , 1 \left.\right)$$
Find the volume of the parallelepiped with one vertex at the origin and adjacent vertices at $$( 1 , 0 , - 3 \left.\right) ,$$ $$(1,2,4)$$ , and $$(5,1,0)$$ .
Find the volume of the parallelepiped with one vertex at the origin and adjacent vertices at $$(1,3,0)$$ , $$( - 2,0,2)$$ , and $$\left( {- 1,3, - 1} \right)$$ .

Use the concept of volume to explain why the determinant of a $$3 \times 3$$ matrix $$A$$ is zero if and only if $$A$$ is not invertible. Do not appeal to Theorem 4 in Section 3.2. [Hint: Think about the columns of $$A$$ .]

Let $$T:\mathbb{R}^{m}\rightarrow\mathbb{R}^{n}$$ be a linear transformation, and let $$\textbf{p}$$ be a vector and $$S$$ a set in $$\mathbb{R}^{m}$$ . Show that the image of $$\textbf{p} + S$$ under $$T$$ is the translated set $$T(\textbf{p}) + T(S)$$ in $$\mathbb{R}^{n}$$ .

Let $$S$$ be the parallelogram determined by the vectors $$\textbf{b}_{1} = \left\lbrack \begin{array}{r} {- 2} \\ 3 \end{array} \right\rbrack$$ and $$\textbf{b}_{2} = \left\lbrack \begin{array}{r} {- 2} \\ 5 \end{array} \right\rbrack$$ , and let $$A = \left\lbrack \begin{array}{rr} 6 & {- 3} \\ {- 3} & 2 \end{array} \right\rbrack$$ . Compute the area of the image of $$S$$ under the mapping $$\textbf{x}\mapsto A\textbf{x}$$ .

Repeat Exercise 27 with $$\textbf{b}_{1} = \left\lbrack \begin{array}{r} 4 \\ {- 7} \end{array} \right\rbrack$$ , $$\textbf{b}_{2} = \left\lbrack \begin{array}{r} 0 \\ 1 \end{array} \right\rbrack$$ , and $$A = \left\lbrack \begin{array}{rr} 5 & 2 \\ 1 & 1 \end{array} \right\rbrack$$ .
Find a formula for the area of the triangle whose vertices are $$\textbf{0}$$ , $$\textbf{v}_{1}$$ , and $$\textbf{v}_{2}$$ in $$\mathbb{R}^{2}$$ .

Let $$R$$ be the triangle with vertices at $$(x_{1},y_{1})$$ , $$(x_{2},y_{2})$$ , and $$(x_{3},y_{3})$$ . Show that $$\left{ \text{area} \text{of} \text{triangle} \right} = \frac{1}{2} \det \begin{bmatrix} x_{1} & y_{1} & 1 \\ x_{2} & y_{2} & 1 \\ x_{3} & y_{3} & 1 \end{bmatrix}$$
[Hint: Translate $$R$$ to the origin by subtracting one of the vertices, and use Exercise 29.]

Let $$T:\mathbb{R}^{3}\rightarrow\mathbb{R}^{3}$$ be the linear transformation determined by the matrix $$A = \left\lbrack \begin{array}{rrr} a & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & b & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & c \end{array} \right\rbrack$$ , where $$a$$ , $$b$$ , and $$c$$ are positive numbers. Let $$S$$ be the unit ball, whose bounding surface has the equation $$x_{1}^{2} + x_{2}^{2} + x_{3}^{2} = 1$$ .

list.item: Show that $$T(S)$$ is bounded by the ellipsoid with the equation $$\frac{x_{1}^{2}}{a^{2}} + \frac{x_{2}^{2}}{b^{2}} + \frac{x_{3}^{2}}{c^{2}} = 1$$ .
Use the fact that the volume of the unit ball is $$4\pi/3$$ to determine the volume of the region bounded by the ellipsoid in part (a).

problem.paragraph: Let $$S$$ be the tetrahedron in $$\mathbb{R}^{3}$$ with vertices at the vectors $$\textbf{0}$$ , $$\textbf{e}_{1}$$ , $$\textbf{e}_{2}$$ , and $$\textbf{e}_{3}$$ , and let $$S^{'}$$ be the tetrahedron with vertices at vectors $$\textbf{0}$$ , $$\textbf{v}_{1}$$ , $$\textbf{v}_{2}$$ , and $$\textbf{v}_{3}$$ . See the figure below.

Let $$A$$ be an $$n \times n$$ matrix. If $$A^{- 1} = \frac{1}{ \text{det} A} \text{adj} A$$ is computed, what should $$AA^{- 1}$$ be equal to in order to confirm that $$A^{- 1}$$ has been found correctly?

If a parallelogram fits inside a circle radius $$1$$ and $$\det A = 2$$ , where $$A$$ is the matrix whose columns correspond to the edges of the parallelogram, does it seem like $$A$$ and its determinant have been calculated correctly to correspond to the area of this parallelogram? Explain why or why not.

image.alt: The figure consists of two parts that illustrate two spatial arrangements of tetrahedrons in three dimensions: one with vertices lying on the three axes and one at the origin, and the other with one vertex at the origin and the others off-axes.

list.item: Describe a linear transformation that maps ﻿ $$S$$ onto $$S^{'}$$ Find a formula for the volume of the tetrahedron $$S^{'}$$ using the fact that $${ \text{volume of} S } = ( 1 / 3 ) \cdot { \text{area of base} } \cdot { \text{height} }$$

exercise_group.instruction: In Exercises 35–38, mark each statement as True or False (T/F). Justify each answer.

problem.paragraph: (T/F) Two parallelograms with the same base and height have the same area.
(T/F) Applying a linear transformation to a region does not change its area.
(T/F) If $$A$$ is an invertible $$n \times n$$ matrix, then $$A^{- 1} = \text{adj} A$$ .
(T/F) Cramer’s rule can only be used for invertible matrices.

[T] Test the inverse formula of Theorem 8 for a random $$4 \times 4$$ matrix $$A$$ . Use your matrix program to compute the cofactors of the $$3 \times 3$$ submatrices, construct the adjugate, and set $$B = \text{(adj} A)/ \text{(det} A)$$ . Then compute $$B - \text{inv} (A)$$ , where $$\text{inv} (A)$$ is the inverse of $$A$$ as computed by the matrix program. Use floating point arithmetic with the maximum possible number of decimal places. Report your results.

[T] Test Cramer’s rule for a random $$4 \times 4$$ matrix $$A$$ and a random $$4 \times 1$$ vector $$\textbf{b}$$ . Compute each entry in the solution of $$A\textbf{x} = \textbf{b}$$ , and compare these entries with the entries in $$A^{- 1}\textbf{b}$$ . Write the command (or keystrokes) for your matrix program that uses Cramer’s rule to produce the second entry of $$\textbf{x}$$ .

[T] If your version of MATLAB has the flops command, use it to count the number of floating point operations to compute $$A^{- 1}$$ for a random $$30 \times 30$$ matrix. Compare this number with the number of flops needed to form $$( \text{adj} A)/(\det A)$$ .
